title: Small-sample 90% t-confidence interval for machine assembly time
scenario_markdown: An industrial engineering department studies the cycle time (in minutes) required to assemble a specialized electronic sensor. A random sample of $n = 10$ assembly runs yields a sample mean of $\bar{x} = 42.3\text{ minutes}$ and a sample standard deviation of $s = 5.1\text{ minutes}$. Historical engineering audits suggest cycle times follow an approximately normal distribution. Construct a $90\%$ confidence interval for the true population mean assembly cycle time $\mu$.
assumptions: Assembly cycle times are approximately normally distributed, satisfying the small-sample normality requirement for the t-distribution
Population standard deviation sigma is unknown, requiring the Student's t-distribution with df = n - 1 = 9
Independent random sample of assembly runs

stages.prompt_markdown: Determine the degrees of freedom $df$ for the Student's $t$-distribution and calculate the standard error of the sample mean $SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}$.

options.hint_markdown: For a single-sample $t$-interval, degrees of freedom equal $n - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9$, not $n$.
The standard error divides $s$ by $\sqrt{n} = \sqrt{10} \approx 3.162$, not by $n = 10$.
Standard error of the sample mean requires dividing $s = 5.1$ by $\sqrt{n} = \sqrt{10}$.

stages.explanation_markdown: For estimating a population mean with unknown $\sigma$, the degrees of freedom are $df = n - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9$. The estimated standard error of the mean is $SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{5.1}{\sqrt{10}} \approx 1.6128\text{ minutes}$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Find the critical value $t_{0.05, 9}$ for a $90\%$ confidence level and compute the margin of error $E = t^* \times SE$.

options.hint_markdown: Because $\sigma$ is unknown and $n = 10$ is small, you must use the $t$-distribution ($t_{0.05, 9} = 1.833$), not the standard normal critical value $z = 1.645$.
With $n = 10$, degrees of freedom are $n - 1 = 9$, giving $t_{0.05, 9} \approx 1.833$, rather than $t_{0.05, 10} = 1.812$.
The question specifies $90\%$ confidence (tail area $\alpha/2 = 0.05$), so $t_{0.05, 9} = 1.833$, not the $95\%$ critical value $t_{0.025, 9} = 2.262$.

stages.explanation_markdown: For $90\%$ confidence, $\alpha = 0.10$ and each tail holds $\alpha/2 = 0.05$. In Excel, `=T.INV.2T(0.10, 9)` yields $t^* \approx 1.8331$. Multiplying by $SE = 1.6128$ gives margin of error $E = 1.8331 \times 1.6128 \approx 2.956\text{ minutes} \approx 2.96\text{ minutes}$.

stages.prompt_markdown: Construct the final $90\%$ confidence interval $\bar{x} \pm E$ and state its statistical interpretation.

options.text_markdown: $[39.34\text{ min}, 45.26\text{ min}]$: We are $90\%$ confident that the true population mean assembly time $\mu$ falls between $39.34$ and $45.26$ minutes.
$[2.14\text{ min}, 8.06\text{ min}]$: We are $90\%$ confident that the true standard deviation falls between $2.14$ and $8.06$ minutes.
options.hint_markdown: A confidence interval for $\mu$ is centered on the sample mean $\bar{x} = 42.3$, not on $s = 5.1$.

options.text_markdown: $[39.65\text{ min}, 44.95\text{ min}]$: We are $90\%$ confident that the true population mean assembly time $\mu$ falls between $39.65$ and $44.95$ minutes.
options.hint_markdown: This interval uses the narrower $z$ margin of error ($2.65$); the wider $t$ margin of error ($2.96$) is required when $\sigma$ is unknown.

options.text_markdown: $[39.34\text{ min}, 45.26\text{ min}]$: There is a $90\%$ probability that a randomly selected individual assembly run will take between $39.34$ and $45.26$ minutes.
options.hint_markdown: A confidence interval for $\mu$ estimates the population mean parameter, not the range containing $90\%$ of individual assembly runs.

stages.explanation_markdown: The confidence interval is $\bar{x} \pm E = 42.3 \pm 2.96 = [39.34, 45.26]\text{ minutes}$. In Excel, the margin of error is directly obtained with `=CONFIDENCE.T(0.10, 5.1, 10)` which returns $2.9564$. We are $90\%$ confident that the true population mean assembly time $\mu$ lies within this range.
